name: Momo Medical
summary: Puts a sensor under nursing-home mattresses so night staff see who needs help.

scene.job: It is a healthcare company that believes in the important role of technology in the healthcare sector.

deep_dive.product: A healthcare company that believes in the important role of technology in the healthcare sector.

title: Momo Medical
research_summary: a healthcare company that believes in the important role of technology in the healthcare sector.
job: Momo Medical puts a sensor under a nursing-home mattress and links it to an app on the night shift. Staff can see who is restless, who is still showing signs of life, and who is about to get out of bed. The company says a personal alert can come up to 70 seconds before a resident leaves the bed. Homes use it so staff skip rounds for people who are sleeping safely.
who_pays: Nursing homes pay a subscription that covers the app, the bed sensors, and the network linking them. No monthly price is published. The company offers a care location three months of the app at no charge.

what_it_does.text: Momo Medical puts a sensor under a nursing-home mattress and links it to an app on the night shift. Staff can see who is restless, who is still showing signs of life, and who is about to get out of bed. The company says a personal alert can come up to 70 seconds before a resident leaves the bed. Homes use it so staff skip rounds for people who are sleeping safely.

who_pays.text: Nursing homes pay a subscription that covers the app, the bed sensors, and the network linking them. No monthly price is published. The company offers a care location three months of the app at no charge.

traction.text: The company's NPEX page says more than 300 Dutch nursing homes use BedSense, plus dozens of homes in North America, Germany, and Belgium, and more than 20,000 residents. Subscriptions passed 14,000 by the end of 2024. Net sales were 2,070,105 euros in 2023, 3,990,659 euros in 2024, and 3,008,600 euros in the first half of 2025. Named users include tanteLouise, which has used it for six years, plus Laurens, Surplus, Allevo, Attent, and UMC Pitman. The NPEX page says falls fell by 28 percent. That figure is the company's own.

why_interesting.text: Sales almost doubled from 2023 to 2024, but the company was still losing money: 1,502,726 euros after tax in 2024 and 699,623 euros in the first half of 2025. In September 2024 it raised 6.5 million euros from PGGM, NextGen Venture, Jay Searson, UNETI Ventures, and the Centre for Aging + Brain Health Innovation, and said it wanted to reach 30,000 beds in Dutch nursing care.

status.text: The product site is taking trial requests, Y Combinator marks the company active, and the NPEX page still publishes results through 30 June 2025. Momo Medical was founded in Delft in 2017 by Menno Gravemaker.

title: Livy Care - HUM Systems
research_summary: The Operating System for Patient Monitoring.
job: Livy Care, made by HUM Systems, is a sensor fixed to the ceiling of a room in a care home or hospital. It notices a fall, a spoken call for help, and warning signs such as sitting on the edge of the bed or getting up, then alerts the nurse. The person does not wear a device or press a button. It can also file blood pressure, pulse, oxygen, weight, blood sugar and detected falls into the care record.
who_pays: Care home groups and hospitals pay. The price is hardware per room, a software licence per sensor, plus setup, training and support, and it depends on how many rooms are fitted and which functions are switched on. No public unit price is listed.

what_it_does.text: Livy Care, made by HUM Systems, is a sensor fixed to the ceiling of a room in a care home or hospital. It notices a fall, a spoken call for help, and warning signs such as sitting on the edge of the bed or getting up, then alerts the nurse. The person does not wear a device or press a button. It can also file blood pressure, pulse, oxygen, weight, blood sugar and detected falls into the care record.

who_pays.text: Care home groups and hospitals pay. The price is hardware per room, a software licence per sensor, plus setup, training and support, and it depends on how many rooms are fitted and which functions are switched on. No public unit price is listed.

traction.text: The company names users including Johannesstift Diakonie, ProCurand, Johanniter senior houses, AWO NOW, Stiftung Kreuznacher Diakonie, Seniorenzentren Linz, Asklepios, MEDICLIN, Klinikum Frankfurt (Oder), GPR Klinikum, St. Marienstift Friesoythe and the von Bodelschwingh foundations Bethel. A study by FH Oberösterreich reported routine checks falling from about 44 hours a week to 19. A University of Bielefeld study reported about 30% less felt workload for staff. Seniorenzentren Linz reported 34% less time on vital signs and 93.63 staff hours saved in a month.

why_interesting.text: A button alarm fails when the person cannot press it, which is common after a fall or in dementia. Livy watches the room instead. The company also says it does not meet the German nurse-call standard DIN VDE 0834, so where that standard is required the sensor sits beside the existing call system rather than replacing it. HUM Systems started with a ceiling smoke alarm sold with Vattenfall, more than 70,000 units, and later turned the same idea toward care.

status.text: The product site is live and lists trade events in October and November 2026, including IFAS in Zurich and the German nursing congress in Berlin. HUM Systems describes itself as based in Berlin, with development in Berlin and Brandenburg.

status.text: As of 5 October 2026 the site is live and says 6Gorilla's and ZHGA are nominated for the Computable Awards 2026. Sigra's site still names 6Gorilla's as its partner for the regional data store.

job: Jubenial lists Spanish homes for owners over 65 who want cash without moving out. In a bare-ownership sale, the owner sells the title and keeps the right to live in the home for life, with no loan and no monthly repayments. The site also lists lifetime-rent deals and small co-investment stakes in housing for older people, and it shows buyers an expected return on each listing. A valuation is free, and nothing is signed until the owner accepts an offer.
who_pays: The older owner is the seller. The buyer is an investor who waits to take full ownership when the lifetime right to live there ends. Jubenial does not publish a fee. A homepage listing showed a flat in Gijón at 157,500 euros against a stated market value of 260,000 euros. The cash the owner receives depends on the home's value and on age.

traction.text: El Referente, updated 11 September 2025, says the project started in August 2023, put out a first version in January 2024, and raised a 100,000 euro pre-seed round in March 2024, after time in La Finca Ventures Camp. The same profile says 2024 revenue beat the first-year plan by more than 76 percent, and it reports a positive result above 40,000 euros on the profit measure it labels EBITDA, and it lists a 2025 company value of 2 million euros. Those figures are from that startup profile, not from accounts I could read. EntreMayores named Rodolfo Nevado and Víctor Tostado as the founders in an 18 October 2024 article.

why_interesting.text: The older the resident, the less the lifetime right to stay is valued, and the more cash the sale pays now. Heirs do not receive the home. They receive whatever money is left. EntreMayores, quoting Nevado, still called lifetime rent and reverse mortgages a small share of Spanish home sales, even as the company builds a list around them.

status.text: The site is listing homes and inviting free valuations. El Referente marked the company open in its 11 September 2025 update, with an address in Pozuelo de Alarcón, Madrid.
